mainTopic: Mixing two methods: a גט validated partly by the שליח and partly by קיום, combining גידוד and מחיצה, and washing hands in halves
overview: A שליח who brings a גט from overseas must say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.' The amud opens with רבא's ruling: if the שליח and another person confirm the second signature, the גט is invalid, so that people will not copy this method for ordinary money documents. רב אשי rejects that reason and says a גט must be validated entirely through regular קיום or entirely through the תקנת חכמים, never a mix. The גמרא reads the משנה of 'בפני נכתב כולו, בפני נחתם חציו' as supporting רבא or רב אשי but not the stricter view of רב חסדא. רב חסדא answers that the משנה uses the style of לא זו אף זו, so the proof falls away. The גמרא then brings related 'halves' cases. For walls on שבת, רב חסדא says a 5-טפח גידוד and a 5-טפח מחיצה do not combine, while מרימר says they do, and the הלכה follows מרימר. Finally, אילפא asks whether hands can become טהור in halves. After rejecting several ways of reading his question, the גמרא limits it to a hand that is still wet, and it begins to challenge that answer from a משנה quoted on the next amud.

steps.title: The agent plus another person confirming the second signature is invalid
steps.stepSummary: If the שליח and another person testify about the second witness's signature, the גט is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he (the agent) and another person testify about the signature of the second witness, the גט is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with רבא's ruling, which began on the previous amud. The שליח's own statement did not cover the second signature, so he and another person try to confirm it the normal way, and רבא rules that this does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally two people confirming a signature is a perfectly good way to verify a document. Here it is ruled invalid anyway. The next step will explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: A handwritten signature
They testify
Invalid

phrases.english: He and another person testify
phrases.notes: 'He' is the שליח who brought the גט.

phrases.english: about the signature of the second witness – it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא וְאַחֵר מְעִידִין עַל חֲתִימַת יַד שֵׁנִי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שליח together with another person may not confirm the second signature; the גט is invalid.

steps.title: The reason: people would confuse this with ordinary documents
steps.stepSummary: Allowing this might lead people to do the same with regular money documents, where most of the money would then be collected on one witness's word.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? People will come to confuse it with the confirming of ordinary documents, and then most of the money (all but a quarter) would be taken out based on the word of one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ruling is so, and answers that it is a protective rule for documents in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ordinary documents, every signature needs two people to confirm it. If one witness confirmed his own signature and also helped confirm the other one, he alone would supply most of the testimony. The חכמים blocked this method in a גט so people would not copy it for money documents.

keyTerms.meaning: They will come to confuse (one case with another)
Confirming documents by verifying the signatures
Minus a quarter (literally)
A witness

phrases.english: What is the reason?
People will come to confuse it
with the confirming of ordinary documents,
and the money, minus a quarter, would be taken out
on the word of one witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? אָתוּ לְאִיחַלּוֹפֵי בְּקִיּוּם שְׁטָרוֹת דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the ruling in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the combination in step 1 is invalid.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a safeguard so people will not use this method for ordinary documents and collect money mostly on one witness's word.

steps.title: רב אשי: can adding a second person make it worse?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects that the שליח alone could have validated everything, so adding another witness should not make the גט invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenged this: Is there such a thing, where if he had finished the whole statement himself, it would be valid, and now that there is one more person with him, it is invalid?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the reason given in step 2. He points out that the result does not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שליח had simply said 'בפני נחתם' about the whole signing, his word alone would make the גט valid. It seems absurd that having an extra person on his side would turn a valid גט into an invalid one. So the 'confusion' reason cannot be the right explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it
Is there such a thing? (a rhetorical challenge)
Statement, declaration
Valid

phrases.english: Rav Ashi challenged this:
Is there such a thing,
that if he himself had completed
the entire statement, it would be valid;
now that there is one more with him, it is invalid?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning of step 2 (fear of confusion with ordinary documents).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Extra support should not weaken what the שליח could have validated alone, so invalidating the גט for that reason is illogical.

steps.title: רב אשי: the גט must be validated entirely one way
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules that even if the שליח is himself the second signer it is invalid, because a גט must rest fully on קיום or fully on the תקנת חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Even if he says 'I am the second witness,' it is invalid. What is the reason? It must be either entirely through confirming the גט, or entirely through the חכמים' enactment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי replaces the earlier reason with his own explanation. His explanation leads to an even stronger ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not confusion. The problem is mixing two different systems. A גט can be validated by ordinary קיום שטרות or by the שליח's special statement, but not by half of one and half of the other. So even when the שליח is one of the signers himself, the mix still fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier approach and offers a new one)
Confirming the גט the regular way, through its signatures
The rabbinic enactment that the שליח's statement validates the גט

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, you cannot mix systems. A גט is validated entirely through regular קיום or entirely through the שליח's statement.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אוֹמֵר ״אֲנִי הוּא עֵד שֵׁנִי״ – פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: Even if he says 'I am the second witness' – it is invalid.
What is the reason?
Either all of it through confirming the גט,
or all of it through the enactment of the חכמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲפִילּוּ אוֹמֵר אֲנִי הוּא עֵד שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the earlier reason, רב אשי gives a new principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט cannot be validated by combining ordinary קיום with the שליח's special statement, even when the שליח is himself a signer.

steps.title: Testing it from the משנה: written fully, signed half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that 'בפני נכתב כולו, בפני נחתם חציו' is invalid, and asks what the case is regarding the other half.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'All of it was written in my presence, half of it was signed in my presence' – it is invalid. The other half, what is the situation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to check רב אשי's principle. It begins by asking what is going on with the half of the signing that the שליח did not see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step sets up the proof. If the other half had some testimony and the גט is still invalid, that would support the rulings of רבא and רב אשי. First the גמרא must pin down the case.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
It was written in my presence
It was signed in my presence
What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: We learned: 'All of it was written in my presence,'
half of it was signed in my presence' – it is invalid.
phrases.notes: 'Half' means he saw only one of the two witnesses sign.

phrases.english: The other half, what is the situation?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: בְּפָנַי נִכְתַּב כּוּלּוֹ, בְּפָנַי נֶחְתַּם חֶצְיוֹ, פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to test רב אשי's principle.
steps.raayaObject: That the גט is invalid even when the other half of the signing has partial testimony, as in the case of רבא (step 1) or רב אשי (step 4).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'בפני נכתב כולו, בפני נחתם חציו – פסול.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the unseen half of the signing is handled in the משנה's case.

steps.title: It can't mean nobody testifies about the other half
steps.stepSummary: If no one confirmed the other half, the ruling would be obvious, since the משנה already invalidates a case with even more testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say no one testifies about it at all, then consider this: when one שליח says 'it was written in my presence' and the other says 'it was signed in my presence,' where this one testifies about all of the writing and that one about all of the signing, it is invalid. Then with only half, do we even need to say it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first way to read the משנה and rejects it, because that reading would make the משנה say something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already rules that splitting the statement between two שלוחים is invalid, even though every part is covered by someone. A case where half the signing is covered by no one at all would surely be invalid too, so the משנה would not need to teach it. This pushes the גמרא toward reading the משנה as a case where the other half did have some testimony behind it, as the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introducing an option that will be rejected)
He testifies
Is it necessary (to say)? Obviously not

steps.confusionAlert: The two-שלוחים case ('one says נכתב, one says נחתם') is a different line of the same משנה. It is quoted here only to show that the half-signed case would be too obvious to teach if no one testified about the other half.

phrases.english: If you say that there is no one
who testifies about it at all;
now, where one says 'it was written in my presence'
and one says 'it was signed in my presence,'
where this one testifies about all of the writing
and that one testifies about all of the signing, it is invalid;
with only half, is it necessary to say?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּלֵיכָּא דְּקָא מַסְהֵיד עֲלֵיהּ כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that no one testifies about the other half of the signatures.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would make the משנה's ruling obvious, since a case with fuller testimony (two שלוחים) is already invalid.

steps.title: The משנה must follow רבא or רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: To avoid the משנה being obvious, the גמרא explains that the other half did have some testimony, like the cases of רבא or רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה is talking either about the case of רבא or about the case of רב אשי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from the last step by saying the משנה must be talking about a case where there was some testimony on the second signature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that if nobody confirmed the second half, the משנה would be teaching nothing new. So the גמרא says the משנה must mean the second signature was backed up in some way: the שליח plus another witness (רבא), or the שליח as the second signer himself (רב אשי). Even so, the גט is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new explanation after rejecting the first
Like the case or view of רבא
Like the case or view of רב אשי

phrases.english: Rather, either like Rava
or like Rav Ashi,
phrases.notes: רב אשי's case: the שליח is himself the second signer (step 4).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אוֹ כִּדְרָבָא אוֹ כִּדְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty in step 6 by redefining the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is talking about a case where nobody confirmed the second half
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about a case with partial testimony on the second signature, like רבא or רב אשי

steps.title: This excludes רב חסדא's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the משנה only supports the smaller חידוש of רבא and רב אשי, not the larger one of רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this rules out the view of רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the last step: the משנה backs רבא or רב אשי, but not רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא says the גט is invalid even when the second signature is fully confirmed by two witnesses, which is a much bigger חידוש. Since the משנה only hints at its חידוש, we can only learn the smaller one from it. If the משנה wanted to teach רב חסדא's big חידוש, it would have said so openly.

keyTerms.meaning: And to exclude; to rule out a different view
אמורא who invalidates the גט even with full confirmation of the second signature

phrases.english: And to exclude the view of Rav Chisda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the reading in step 7 against רב חסדא
steps.raayaObject: That רב חסדא's broad ruling is not taught by the משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of 'בפני נחתם חציו', which only hints at a small חידוש

steps.title: רב חסדא points to another 'extra' line in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא counters that by the same logic, the line 'נכתב בפני אבל לא נחתם בפני' would also be unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא could answer you: According to your logic, why do I need the line 'It was written in my presence but not signed in my presence'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא pushes back by showing that the משנה has another line that also looks unneeded. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה already says that 'half signed in my presence' is invalid, then 'not signed in my presence at all' is obviously invalid too. Yet the משנה still says it. So the משנה clearly includes lines that seem extra, which weakens the argument from step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you; introduces a defense on someone's behalf
And according to your own reasoning; turns the argument back on the asker
Why do I need it? Asks why something is said if it seems extra

phrases.english: Rav Chisda could say to you:
And according to your reasoning,
'It was written in my presence but not signed in my presence'
why do I need it?
phrases.notes: If even 'half signed' is invalid, then 'not signed at all' is obviously invalid, so why say it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind step 8 that every line in the משנה must teach something new
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference in step 8 that the משנה line must be teaching an extra חידוש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה clearly contains another line that seems unneeded, so seeming extra is not proof of a hidden חידוש

steps.title: The משנה teaches 'not only this, but also that'
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the משנה often lists a smaller case and then a bigger one, so no proof against him can be drawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה teaches in the style of 'not only this, but also that.' Here too, it teaches 'not only this, but also that.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives his answer: the extra-looking line is just the משנה's normal style of building from a smaller case to a bigger one, so the proof against him falls away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the style called לא זו אף זו, the משנה states an easier case and then adds a harder one, even if the harder one alone would have been enough. So the line 'בפני נחתם חציו' does not need a hidden extra case of testimony. That means it cannot be used to rule out רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: Not only this, but also that; a style of building from a smaller case to a bigger one
It teaches; refers to how the משנה is worded
Here too; applies the same idea to the case at hand

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא tried to use the משנה to back רבא and רב אשי against רב חסדא. רב חסדא answers that the משנה uses the 'לא זו אף זו' style, so a line that seems extra proves nothing, and his view still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: 'לא זו אף זו' does not mean the first case is wrong. Both cases are true; the משנה just moves from the smaller חידוש to the bigger one.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לֹא זוֹ אַף זוֹ קָתָנֵי,
phrases.english: Rather, it teaches 'not only this, but also that,'
here too
phrases.notes: He means the line 'בפני נחתם חציו' that the proof was built on.

phrases.english: it teaches 'not only this, but also that.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לֹא זוֹ אַף זוֹ קָתָנֵי, הָכָא נָמֵי לָא זוֹ אַף זוֹ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's counter-argument from step 9 and rejects the proof in step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה against רב חסדא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed every seemingly extra line must hide a new חידוש, but the משנה often uses the לא זו אף זו style
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general rule for reading the משנה: a line that looks extra is not always a source for a hidden חידוש, because of the לא זו אף זו style.

steps.title: An embankment and a wall do not combine
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that 5 טפחים of embankment plus 5 טפחים of wall do not combine into a 10-טפח מחיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: an embankment of five handbreadths and a partition of five handbreadths do not join together. The ten must be entirely partition or entirely embankment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ruling of רב חסדא about שבת domains. The case is a 10-טפח boundary made half from a drop in the ground and half from a built wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחיצה must be 10 טפחים high to enclose a רשות היחיד. רב חסדא says two different kinds of barrier cannot be added together; all ten must be one kind. This matches the idea from the גט discussion that something must be fully established one way or fully the other way.

keyTerms.meaning: An embankment, meaning a difference in ground height, like the edge of a pit or a slope
A partition or wall
They join together or combine
A handbreadth (a 10-טפח height is the minimum for a halachic wall)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
An embankment of five [handbreadths]
phrases.notes: This is about the walls of a private domain on שבת, which must be ten handbreadths high.

phrases.english: and a partition of five
do not join together
unless it is either entirely partition
or entirely embankment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: גִּידּוּד חֲמִשָּׁה וּמְחִיצָה חֲמִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related case brought because it shares the 'two halves combining' idea with the גט discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A 5-טפח גידוד and a 5-טפח מחיצה do not combine; the 10 טפחים must all be one kind.

steps.title: מרימר says they do combine
steps.stepSummary: מרימר taught the opposite: the embankment and the wall do combine into 10 טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר taught: an embankment of five and a partition of five do join together.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר gives a ruling that disagrees with רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the same case, מרימר holds that height is height. Five טפחים of drop plus five טפחים of wall add up to a valid 10-טפח מחיצה.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught publicly or expounded

phrases.english: Mareimar taught publicly:
An embankment of five and a partition of five
join together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An opposing opinion to רב חסדא's ruling in Step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A 5-טפח גידוד and a 5-טפח מחיצה combine into a 10-טפח partition.

steps.title: The הלכה: they combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like מרימר: the embankment and the wall combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: they join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the dispute and rules like מרימר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, a mixed boundary of גידוד and מחיצה totaling 10 טפחים counts as a valid wall for שבת. רב חסדא's 'all one kind' approach is not followed in this area.

keyTerms.meaning: And the practical הלכה is

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא says an embankment and a wall don't combine; מרימר says they do, and the הלכה follows מרימר.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though רב חסדא's view lines up with the 'all one way' idea from the גט discussion, the halacha for walls on שבת goes the other way.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: they join together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute between Steps 11 and 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הלכה follows מרימר: גידוד and מחיצה combine to make 10 טפחים.

steps.title: אילפא asks whether hands become pure in halves
steps.stepSummary: אילפא asks whether hands can become טהור through washing done 'in halves.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אילפא asked: are hands made pure in halves, or are they not made pure in halves?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another 'halves' question, this time about נטילת ידים. It is setting up the next moves, where the גמרא tries to figure out what case אילפא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether a washing split into two partial parts can count as one complete washing. אילפא leaves the case undefined, so the גמרא will need to clarify it.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, raising an unresolved question (בעיא)
In halves
Ritually pure

phrases.english: Ilfa asked:
Hands: are they made pure in halves,
or are they not made pure in halves?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case built on the same 'halves combining' idea
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a washing of the hands done in two partial parts make them טהור?

steps.title: Not two people sharing one רביעית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests אילפא meant two people washing from one רביעית, but a משנה already says that works.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If we say two people wash from one רביעית, didn't we learn: from a רביעית one may wash the hands of one person, and even of two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case אילפא means and tries a first suggestion. It rejects the suggestion right away from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each of two people uses half a רביעית, each hand-washing is a 'half.' But the משנה in ידים already says a רביעית is enough even for two people. So אילפא could not have asked about this.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the details?
A quarter-לוג, the standard amount of water for washing hands
If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)
One washes the hands

phrases.english: What is the case?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא דְּקָא מָשׁוּ בֵּי תְרֵי מֵרְבִיעִית,
phrases.english: If we say that two people wash from one revi'is,
but didn't we learn in a משנה:
from a revi'is one may wash the hands
for one person, and even for two!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִילֵּימָא דְּקָא מָשׁוּ בֵּי תְרֵי מֵרְבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to define אילפא's case and rejects the first option
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that אילפא was asking about two people sharing one רביעית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה explicitly allows two people to wash from one רביעית, so there would be nothing to ask.

steps.title: Not washing one hand at a time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests אילפא meant washing each hand separately, but a משנה says even different methods for each hand work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where he washes each hand one at a time. But didn't we learn: one who washes one hand by pouring and one hand by dipping, his hands are pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second way to explain אילפא's case and rejects it too with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing each hand separately could be called purifying 'in halves.' But the משנה rules that one hand washed from a vessel and the other dipped in a river are both טהור. So washing hands separately is clearly fine, and that also can't be אילפא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather (offering a new suggestion)
Washing by pouring water from a vessel
Purifying by dipping the hand into water, like a river

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא דְּקָא מָשֵׁי חֲדָא חֲדָא יְדֵיהּ,
phrases.english: But rather, where he washes his hands one at a time,
but didn't we learn in a משנה:
one who does one hand by pouring
and the other one by dipping,
his hands are pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא דְּקָא מָשֵׁי חֲדָא חֲדָא יְדֵיהּ, וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first explanation was rejected in Step 15, the גמרא offers a second explanation and rejects it too
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that אילפא was asking about washing one hand at a time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה allows each hand to be purified separately, even by different methods, so there would be nothing to ask.

steps.title: A third reading of אילפא's question, and an immediate problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests אילפא meant washing half of one hand and then the other half. But דבי רבי ינאי taught that hands cannot become טהור in halves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps he means a case where a person washes his hand half at a time. But didn't the school of רבי ינאי say: hands do not become pure in halves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third way to understand אילפא's question: one hand washed in two separate halves. It immediately attacks this reading with a known teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time 'halves' means one single hand washed in two parts, not two people or two hands. But דבי רבי ינאי already said this kind of washing does not work. So if the answer is already known, what was אילפא asking?

keyTerms.meaning: Half by half. Washing one part of the hand, then the other part.
Washes
The school (students) of רבי ינאי
In halves

phrases.english: But rather, where he washes
his hand half by half,
But didn't the school of רבי ינאי say:
Hands do not become pure in halves!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא דְּקָא מָשֵׁי פַּלְגָא פַּלְגָא דְּיָדֵיהּ, וְהָאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 16 rejected the 'each hand separately' reading, this offers a third reading and challenges it as well.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that אילפא asked about washing one hand in two halves.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דבי רבי ינאי already ruled that hands cannot become טהור in halves, so there would be nothing left to ask.

steps.title: The question is about a hand that is still wet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אילפא's question is only about a case where the first washed half is still wet when the second half is washed.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the question is needed for a case where there is still moist liquid on the hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves the third reading by narrowing it. אילפא was asking about a special case where the hand is still wet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary half-washing fails, as רבי ינאי's school said. But if the water from the first half is still wet on the hand, maybe it connects with the second washing and counts as one washing. That was a real question.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for... (narrows the case)
Liquid that is still moist, wet enough to wet something else

phrases.english: No, it is needed where there is moist liquid.
phrases.notes: The water from washing the first half is still wet on the hand when he washes the second half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 by limiting אילפא's question to a case with leftover moisture.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אילפא's question was already answered by דבי רבי ינאי's rule against washing in halves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers ordinary half-washing. אילפא asked whether leftover wetness joins the two halves into one washing.

steps.title: Why should wetness make a difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer: what difference does moist liquid make? It begins to quote a משנה to show that wetness does not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if there is moist liquid, what of it? But didn't we learn in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether leftover wetness could matter at all. It starts quoting a משנה as proof; the משנה itself is quoted on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 18 assumes wetness might join the two halves. The גמרא now doubts that, and it is preparing to show from a משנה that moisture alone does not create a connection. The proof itself comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What difference does it make?
But didn't we learn in a משנה?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי אִיכָּא מַשְׁקֶה טוֹפֵחַ מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: And when there is moist liquid, what of it?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אִיכָּא מַשְׁקֶה טוֹפֵחַ מַאי הָוֵי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 18 and sets up a proof from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 18 that leftover moisture might join the two halves of the washing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Moist liquid should not make a difference, and a משנה (quoted next) will show this.
